question: Exec is ~76% of a cold go build. What is the 129 ms made of?
finding: The per-exec cost is three separable terms, not one. (1) fork alone is 4.25 ms against Docker's 0.15 ms - 28x before any image work happens. (2) exec adds a FIXED ~18 ms independent of guest size, which is carrick self-re-execing its own ~30 MB signed binary and rebuilding dispatcher state from the capsule. (3) on top of that a size-linear ~2.6 ms/MB, which is materializing the guest image - 52 ms of `compile`'s 125 ms.
translation_is_not_the_term: Shared translation removes 87% of translations on this workload (170,727 -> 22,895) and buys only 3.3% of wall, because its own load costs 14.8 ms per process. So per-exec cost is dominated by process and image setup, NOT by translating guest code. This corrects the intuition the codegen campaign was built on.

shared_translation_load.note: ~2.4 ms/MB for a 6 MB unit - the same ~400 MB/s constant as image materialization, i.e. page-fault plus code-signature validation of a signed Mach-O dylib, not dyld CPU (dyld is 1.5% of profile). Units are signed dylibs loaded with dlopen; publishing shells out to /usr/bin/codesign twice.

caveat: All rows in-guest wall, container lifecycle excluded, carrick and docker phases run serially. `( : )` is a subshell fork with no exec; `/bin/true` is fork+exec of a 68 KB dynamically linked binary.
